findings.title: Required statistical sensitivity analysis is not evidenced
findings.impact: The statistics_reporting role cannot independently validate the high-risk production claim's required coverage of missingness, exclusion, denominator, and sensitivity behavior. The pilot report appropriately suppresses inference, but that does not establish sensitivity reporting across supported production workflows.
evidence: audits/agent_charters/statistics_reporting.md:7-8 requires formulas, denominators, missingness, multiplicity correction, effect sizes, confidence intervals, and sensitivity analyses.
audits/evidence/v571_rc5_candidate/report/report_metadata.json:5-13 documents only two specimens and no inferential or secondary tests.
audits/evidence/v571_rc5_candidate/report/01_biological_results/data/biological_statistical_tests.csv:2-8 contains no sensitivity-analysis fields or results.
findings.recommendation: Add retained, independently reviewable specimen-level sensitivity outputs covering applicable exclusion/QC, missingness, and normalization scenarios, or narrow the production claim so it does not assert complete statistical-reporting coverage.

limitations: The retained biological evidence contains one KJ and one WT specimen, so it cannot establish a group effect or validate inferential behavior at the required minimum of three specimens per group.
No PDF visual inspection was performed; numerical agreement was accepted only from the retained pypdf token-validation artifact.
No full-stack inference was run, per instruction.
recommended_follow_up: Provide an append-only remediation evidence artifact with specimen-level sensitivity analyses and independent statistical review.
Keep the explicit insufficient-specimens status and prohibition on biological group-effect claims for the current pilot.
